question: A 29-year-old man comes to the emergency department because of progressively worsening fatigue and shortness of breath for the past 2 weeks. His only medication is insulin. Examination shows elevated jugular venous distention and coarse crackles in both lungs. Despite appropriate life-saving measures, he dies. Gross examination of the heart at autopsy shows concentrically thickened myocardium and microscopic examination shows large cardiomyocytes with intracellular iron granules. Examination of the spinal cord shows atrophy of the lateral corticospinal tracts, spinocerebellar tracts, and dorsal columns. Which of the following is the most likely underlying cause of this patient's condition?

options.opb: CTG trinucleotide repeat expansion on chromosome 19
options.opc: Dystrophin gene mutation on the X chromosome
options.opd: GAA trinucleotide repeat expansion on chromosome 9

enhanced_information: The most likely underlying cause of this patient's condition is opd. GAA trinucleotide repeat expansion on chromosome 9, leading to Friedreich ataxia. The reasoning chain aligns with the presentation of cardiomyopathy, iron overload, neurological complications, and spinal cord atrophy seen in this patient.
analysis: The patient's presentation with cardiomyopathy, iron overload, and neurological complications, specifically spinal cord atrophy, is highly suggestive of Friedreich ataxia. Friedreich ataxia is caused by a GAA trinucleotide repeat expansion on chromosome 9. This expansion leads to frataxin deficiency, resulting in mitochondrial dysfunction and subsequent tissue damage, explaining the cardiac and neurological findings in this patient.
